2) Recommended timeout/retry matrix and a sample backoff implementation we can drop into our client code.

Alex — thanks, great summary. Attaching a compact cutover checklist and a small SDK snippets bundle. Below are the recommended guardrails we use with most customers; happy to tailor during the sandbox run.

Quick checklist (high level)
- Pick SDK v3.1.0 (backwards compatible) and validate env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (sandbox/prod), REDWOOD_REGION.
- Integrate request-id and idempotency-key headers. Use UUID v4 for every client request.
- Start in sandbox with 1% production traffic using header routing and canary checks (3 days).
- Warm KV cache by replaying recent queries (safe replay mode) during low-traffic window.
- Validate P95 and error-rate thresholds; set automatic fallback to cache when 5xx rate > 1% sustained over 5m.

Recommended client-side defaults
- Socket timeout: 10s
- Per-request deadline: 30s (includes retries)
- Retries: 3 attempts max
- Retry backoff: exponential with full jitter: backoff_ms = random_between(0, base * 2^attempt) with base=200ms
- Idempotency: if request is non-idempotent (writes), require idempotency-key header to prevent duplication on retries.

Small Node.js retry example (drop-in):
const fetchWithRetries = async (url, opts = {}) => {
  const maxAttempts = 3;
  const base = 200;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, opts);
      if (res.status >= 500) throw new Error('server-error');
      return res;
    } catch (err) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * base * Math.pow(2, attempt);
      if (attempt === maxAttempts - 1) throw err;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, jitter));
    }
  }
};

> Chloe's checklist + Node retry sample pasted above.

Adding infra guidance and precise rate/timeout knobs from the serving side:

Serving-side recommendations - Per-route soft quota: set initial cap = 2x expected steady-state RPS during canary to avoid sudden throttles.
- Burst window: allow short spikes for 30s then throttle to cap.
- Circuit soft-fail behavior: when 5xx rate > 1% or latency P95 rises by 2x for more than 3m, flag route for cache-fallback (client should detect and serve cached content).
- Tokenization: we recommend sending token estimates in header X-Token-Estimate to help the router pick an optimal kernel path.

Retry policy (more concrete)
- For 429: retry with exponential backoff + capped max wait 10s. If repeated 429 within 60s, escalate to token bucket fallback (serve cached response or degraded route).
- For 5xx: retry up to 2 times with backoff; for systemic 5xxs (>1% over 5m) trigger automatic canary rollback.

Client sample: cURL with observability headers
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)" 
  -H "X-Customer-Id: peregrine-123" 
  -H "X-Token-Estimate: 360" 
  -d '{"input":"..."}'

Operational notes for cutover
- Warm KV cache by replaying the last 48 hours of non-sensitive queries in sandbox. Use a conservative throttle (1 QPS per worker).
- Add a short-lived debug flag during the first day of cutover to increase logging to TRACE for failing routes only (costs extra ingestion).
- We can provision a temporary burst pool if you expect high fanout during the cutover window. Let us know if you need a 24-hour burst.

Happy to join the cutover runbook call on 2026-09-28.

Alex / Maria — looping in answers and next steps.

Short answers to the security checklist:
- Log retention: request metadata (headers, status codes, latency) retained for 90 days by default; can be shortened to 30/7 days on enterprise plans.
- Request bodies: not stored by default for hosted API; if you opt-in to request logging (for debug), bodies are redacted unless you enable full payload logging in the console (enterprise customers only).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for Private and Dedicated customers. For hosted customers we offer a CMK add-on with key-wrapping support — we can share the onboarding form.

Alerting / SLO window:
- We can enable an integration that posts to your PagerDuty/Slack channel for sustained 5xx or quota trips during the first 7 days post-cutover. We'll set the default trigger to: 5xx rate > 1% for 5 minutes or quota tripped 3x in 15 minutes.

Next steps (mutual action plan)
- This week: Peregrine to run sandbox canary with SDK snippets (dev team).
- 2026-09-28: Cutover dry-run call (Redwood + Peregrine SRE + CS).
- 2026-09-29: Production cutover during maintenance window.
- Post-cutover (first 7 days): Redwood to enable alerting integration and elevated support.

I have added these to the HubSpot deal (PD-3481) and attached the cutover checklist. Chloe will schedule the dry-run call and send calendar invites.
